problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: prove in arbitrary coordinates that the covariant divergence of a vector obeys ∇_a V^a = (-g)^(-1/2) ∂_μ[(-g)^(1/2)V^μ].
problems.short_topic: Coordinate formula for covariant divergence
problems.disposition_rationale: A compact Chapter 4 exercise connecting the Levi-Civita connection and determinant identity to a coordinate-invariant divergence.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: prove Cartan's formula for the Lie derivative of an arbitrary p-form, L_X Y = i_X dY + d(i_X Y), using the definitions supplied on the sheet.
problems.short_topic: Cartan formula for differential forms
problems.disposition_rationale: This self-contained differential-form identity is a useful Chapter 4 parent and later supports the sheet's symmetry calculations.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: for a conformal Killing vector, prove conservation of its contraction with the tangent to an affinely parameterized null geodesic, and prove that conformal Killing vectors are preserved when g_ab is rescaled to Ω²g_ab.
problems.short_topic: Conformal Killing vectors and null geodesics
problems.disposition_rationale: The two linked claims give a clean Chapter 13 application of conformal symmetry to null propagation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4, parts (a)-(f): starting from the printed static spherical metric, mass function, perfect-fluid stress tensor, and TOV equations, derive the stated monotonic-density inequalities, integrate the comparison equation, control the central-pressure term, and obtain Buchdahl's compactness bound. Retain every intermediate bound and equality condition printed in the six-part chain.
problems.short_topic: Buchdahl compactness inequality from the TOV equations
problems.disposition_rationale: A substantial Chapter 11 stellar-structure parent whose value is the complete comparison proof; extracting only the final inequality would destroy its logic.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 5: solve the TOV system for an incompressible constant-density star, determine the pressure including its central value, and show directly that regularity enforces M/R < 4/9 as the limiting central pressure diverges.
problems.short_topic: Interior Schwarzschild solution and central-pressure bound
problems.disposition_rationale: This explicit Chapter 11 model complements the general Buchdahl proof while remaining a complete, independently usable parent.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 6: introduce T by dT = dt + F(r)dr in Schwarzschild spacetime, choose both signs of F so constant-T slices are flat, write the resulting Painlevé-Gullstrand metrics, and explain which horizon each sign crosses regularly.
problems.short_topic: Painlevé-Gullstrand coordinates for Schwarzschild spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: A concise Chapter 8 coordinate-extension problem that ties a geometric slicing condition to horizon regularity and the ingoing/outgoing sign choice.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 7: analyze null geodesics sent from infinity toward a Schwarzschild black hole, find the critical impact parameter for capture, explain the apparent absorption-disc geometry, and calculate the high-frequency absorption cross-section 27πM².
problems.short_topic: Schwarzschild photon capture cross-section
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 8 parent combines the null effective potential with a directly interpretable observable and should retain the geometric cross-section argument.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 8: model the surface of a collapsing pressureless spherical star as a radial Schwarzschild geodesic released from rest at r_0, then use advanced Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates to calculate the proper times to r = 2M and r = 0 and show that the advanced coordinate v remains finite at the singularity.
problems.short_topic: Radial dust collapse in advanced coordinates
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 11 collapse exercise that cleanly separates finite infalling proper time from the behavior of horizon-regular coordinates.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 9: use the Kruskal form of Schwarzschild spacetime to prove that every future-directed timelike curve in region II reaches the singularity within proper time πM, and identify the limiting curve that saturates the bound.
problems.short_topic: Upper bound on proper time inside Schwarzschild
problems.disposition_rationale: This global Chapter 8 result gives a sharp invariant statement about the black-hole interior, beyond a coordinate-specific geodesic computation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 10: in part (a), use isotropic Schwarzschild coordinates to isometrically embed the constant-time Einstein-Rosen bridge in Euclidean four-space, construct the requested sketch, and discuss whether the bridge is traversable; in part (b), analyze the geometry of constant-r cylinders in Kruskal regions II and III.
problems.short_topic: Einstein-Rosen bridge and Schwarzschild interior cylinders
problems.disposition_rationale: The embedding, constructed sketch, causal interpretation, and interior comparison form one visual-geometric Chapter 8 parent; no source figure is supplied.

problems.parent_scope: Complete starred Question 11, parts (a)-(b): vary the printed Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton action with its exponential scalar coupling to derive all field equations, then verify the complete stated magnetically charged dilaton black-hole metric, gauge field, and scalar solution with its parameter relations.
problems.short_topic: Magnetically charged Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black hole
problems.disposition_rationale: A technically demanding but self-contained Chapter 12 parent linking action variation to an exact nonvacuum black-hole solution.

problems.parent_scope: Complete starred Question 12: for the printed Lifshitz-type metric, show that orthonormal-frame Riemann components and scalar curvature invariants remain finite at r = 0, while freely falling observers experience divergent tidal forces there when z ≠ 1.
problems.short_topic: Nonscalar tidal singularity in a Lifshitz metric
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 6 curvature problem sharply distinguishes bounded invariants from physically divergent parallel-propagated components.

documents.document_locator: Part III Black Holes, sheet code 3R3b

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: for the printed general static, spherically symmetric metric with a simple zero of f at r = r_+, derive radial null curves t ± r_* = constant, show r_* tends to minus infinity at the horizon, and construct an ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinate in which the metric extends analytically across the future horizon.
problems.short_topic: Eddington-Finkelstein extension of a general static horizon
problems.disposition_rationale: A general Chapter 8 horizon-extension parent that reveals which features are local consequences of a simple zero rather than peculiarities of Schwarzschild.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: hold a particle static outside Schwarzschild by a massless inelastic string extending to infinity; compare the local radial force and redshifted work under a displacement, determine the conserved energy and string tension, and take the horizon limits as measured both at the particle and by an observer at infinity.
problems.short_topic: Redshifted force and work near a Schwarzschild horizon
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 8 parent gives an operational account of gravitational redshift through force, energy, and work, with the two observer viewpoints kept together.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: transform a constant-Schwarzschild-time spatial slice to isotropic coordinates, show that each asymptotic end is flat at large radius, and verify that the slice's extrinsic curvature K_ab vanishes.
problems.short_topic: Time-symmetric isotropic Schwarzschild initial data
problems.disposition_rationale: A concise Chapter 8 bridge between the Schwarzschild solution and its two-ended, time-symmetric initial-data geometry.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4, parts (a)-(c): determine D^+(S) and J^+(S) for the specified subsets of the two-dimensional Einstein static universe, repeat after the stated point is removed, and find the corresponding future sets for the t = 0 surface in exterior region I of the Kruskal diagram, constructing causal diagrams as needed.
problems.short_topic: Domains of dependence and causal futures
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 2 parent tests global causal definitions in three deliberately contrasting spacetimes; the puncture and Kruskal cases should not be separated.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 5: derive the necessary and sufficient inequalities on a perfect fluid's density and pressure for the dominant, weak, null, and strong energy conditions, then apply every condition to a cosmological-constant stress tensor for both signs of the cosmological constant.
problems.short_topic: Energy conditions for perfect fluids and vacuum energy
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete Chapter 7 classification that clarifies both logical relations among energy conditions and the exceptional role of vacuum energy.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 6: prove that conformally related metrics have the same unparameterized null geodesics, use the Ricci-tensor transformation printed on the sheet, and determine the curvature-coupling coefficient ξ for which the massless scalar equation (□ - ξR)φ = 0 is conformally covariant, including the scalar's conformal weight.
problems.short_topic: Conformal null geodesics and conformally coupled scalar field
problems.disposition_rationale: The geodesic and field-equation halves form a coherent Chapter 6 exercise on conformal geometry; the supplied Ricci transformation is integral source data.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 7: recognize the printed Robinson-Bertotti metric as AdS2 × S2, introduce null coordinates and then compactified U,V coordinates to find its maximal extension, draw the Penrose diagram, and determine whether the spacetime is globally hyperbolic.
problems.short_topic: Maximal extension of Robinson-Bertotti spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 13 product-spacetime parent combining coordinate extension, causal compactification, and a global-hyperbolicity judgment.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 8: use the supplied conformal relation between de Sitter space and the Einstein static universe to construct the de Sitter Penrose diagram and identify its conformal boundaries and causal structure.
problems.short_topic: Conformal diagram of de Sitter spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: A focused Chapter 16 exercise whose required diagram makes the global structure of de Sitter space explicit.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 9: start from the stated asymptotic form of the unphysical metric near future null infinity, recover the physical large-r metric, shift the radial coordinate to arrange g_uu = -1 + O(1/r), and transform to asymptotically inertial coordinates to show g_μν = η_μν + O(1/r).
problems.short_topic: Asymptotic flatness from conformal null infinity
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 10 parent links conformal completion to the familiar inertial-coordinate falloff and preserves the necessary radial gauge adjustment.

documents.document_locator: Part III Black Holes, sheet code 3R3c

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1, parts (a)-(e): construct the two future null normals to a spacelike two-surface, derive their expansions and rescaling behavior, define trapped and marginal surfaces, show that a marginal surface in time-symmetric initial data is minimal, and extend the expansion formula to general initial data with nonzero K_ab, retaining the printed Kerr-motivated form.
problems.short_topic: Null expansions, trapped surfaces, and apparent horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete Chapter 11 parent that builds apparent-horizon geometry from first principles and connects the time-symmetric and rotating-data cases.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: write the Reissner-Nordström solution in advanced Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, construct its maximally extended Finkelstein/Penrose diagram with all horizon and singularity regions labeled, and prove that r decreases along every future-directed causal curve between the outer and inner horizons.
problems.short_topic: Causal structure of Reissner-Nordström spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: The coordinate form, complete diagram, and monotonicity proof together make a strong Chapter 8 global-structure parent.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3, parts (a)-(e): use Cartan's formula (explicitly referenced to Sheet 1, Question 2) to choose a symmetry-adapted electromagnetic potential; derive the conserved canonical quantity for a charged particle; obtain the radial equation in Reissner-Nordström; analyze extremal static force balance; and determine the charged Penrose energy-extraction condition. The cross-sheet Cartan identity is a declared dependency.
problems.short_topic: Charged-particle motion and energy extraction in Reissner-Nordström
problems.disposition_rationale: A coherent Chapter 8 parent linking electromagnetic symmetry, conserved energy, extremal balance, and a charged analogue of the Penrose process; its stated prior-sheet identity must travel with it.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: transform the printed Kerr-Newman metric from Boyer-Lindquist to ingoing Kerr coordinates, determine the transformation functions, show regularity at the outer horizon, derive the horizon generator's condition, and calculate the horizon area in the stated parameterization.
problems.short_topic: Horizon-regular Kerr-Newman coordinates and area
problems.disposition_rationale: This complete Chapter 8 calculation connects a coordinate extension to invariant horizon data and must retain the supplied full metric.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 5: optimize a single-particle Penrose process in extremal Kerr spacetime and derive the maximum possible energy-extraction efficiency, retaining the horizon kinematics and fragment constraints stated on the sheet.
problems.short_topic: Maximum efficiency of the Penrose process
problems.disposition_rationale: A bounded Chapter 8 optimization problem giving a quantitative consequence of negative-energy states in the Kerr ergoregion.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 6, parts (a)-(e): orient the Kerr horizon and its surface element, relate flux of Killing energy to the horizon generator, establish the sign restrictions for matter satisfying the null energy condition, and apply the result to a scalar mode with frequency ω and azimuthal number ν to derive the superradiant range 0 < ω < νΩ_H. Retain all printed orientation and mode-normalization hints.
problems.short_topic: Horizon energy flux and scalar superradiance
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 8 parent develops superradiance from covariant flux geometry rather than quoting the final frequency inequality.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 7: evaluate the ADM mass of Reissner-Nordström and the electric charge, magnetic charge, Komar mass, and Komar angular momentum of Kerr-Newman using the definitions and asymptotic surface integrals printed on the sheet.
problems.short_topic: ADM, electromagnetic, and Komar charges of black holes
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 7 inventory of conserved gravitational and electromagnetic charges that makes their normalization and asymptotic definitions concrete.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 8: prove the Lichnerowicz no-soliton theorem for a globally stationary, asymptotically flat vacuum spacetime by relating its Komar and ADM masses and invoking the positive-energy theorem under the hypotheses stated on the sheet.
problems.short_topic: Lichnerowicz no-soliton theorem
problems.disposition_rationale: The decisive step is an invocation of the major positive-energy theorem rather than a result developed in the parent; without importing that theorem and its equality case, the exercise is not self-contained enough for reservation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 9, parts (a)-(e): analyze radial null rays in global AdS4; compactify with r = ℓ tan χ and draw its causal diagram; decide global hyperbolicity; define and evaluate the AdS-subtracted Komar mass; and for Schwarzschild-AdS determine the horizon relation and surface gravity as functions of M, ℓ, and r_+.
problems.short_topic: Global AdS and Schwarzschild-AdS black holes
problems.disposition_rationale: This substantial Chapter 16 parent unifies AdS causal structure, asymptotic mass subtraction, and black-hole thermodynamic geometry.

problems.parent_scope: Complete starred Question 10: use curvature invariants of the full Kerr-Newman geometry to locate and characterize its ring curvature singularity, distinguishing it from coordinate singularities at the horizons.
problems.short_topic: Kerr-Newman ring curvature singularity
problems.disposition_rationale: A technically advanced Chapter 8 curvature diagnostic that isolates the genuine singular set of the rotating charged solution.

documents.document_locator: Part III Black Holes, sheet code 3R3d

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1, including parts (a)(i)-(ii) and (b)-(d): establish the Frobenius and Killing-horizon identities printed on the sheet, relate the gradient of surface gravity to curvature, prove constancy along generators and cross-sections, and combine Einstein's equation with the dominant energy condition to complete the zeroth-law proof. Retain all intermediate tensor identities and causal-orientation assumptions.
problems.short_topic: Zeroth law of black-hole mechanics
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete Chapter 8 proof parent; its geometric identities, field-equation step, and energy-condition argument are inseparable from the conclusion that κ is constant.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: apply Stokes' theorem to the Komar integrals in a stationary axisymmetric black-hole spacetime with matter, track the horizon and infinity boundary terms, and derive the stated generalized Smarr relation containing κA, Ω_HJ, and the bulk matter-current contribution.
problems.short_topic: Smarr relation with matter sources
problems.disposition_rationale: This Chapter 7 parent turns conserved-current identities into a global mass formula and keeps the matter term explicit.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: for a stationary axisymmetric Einstein-Maxwell black hole, prove that the co-rotating electric potential -χ^aA_a is constant over the Killing horizon, retaining the gauge and regularity assumptions, and evaluate Φ_H explicitly for the printed Kerr-Newman potential and horizon generator.
problems.short_topic: Constant horizon electrostatic potential
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 8 electromagnetic analogue of the zeroth law that joins the general horizon proof to its Kerr-Newman value.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: specialize the matter Smarr formula to Einstein-Maxwell theory and derive M = κA/(4π) + 2Ω_HJ + Φ_HQ, using the printed hint L_ξ(F^{ab}A_b) = 0 and retaining all horizon and infinity electromagnetic boundary terms.
problems.short_topic: Einstein-Maxwell Smarr formula
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong Chapter 7 application of Noether/Komar reasoning; the supplied Lie-derivative identity and conversion of the bulk term to Φ_HQ are essential.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 5: starting from canonical equal-time commutation relations for a free scalar field, smear the field and momentum with the specified mode functions and derive the creation-annihilation commutators and normalization relations printed on the sheet.
problems.short_topic: Canonical scalar-field mode commutators
problems.disposition_rationale: This is primarily a quantum-field-theory quantization exercise rather than a general-relativity exercise suitable for the Weinberg GR chapter set.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 6: for Klein-Gordon solutions on a stationary spacetime, prove that the Lie derivative along a timelike Killing field is anti-Hermitian with respect to the printed Klein-Gordon inner product and show that positive-frequency modes have positive norm under the stated assumptions.
problems.short_topic: Klein-Gordon norm and positive frequency
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent belongs to quantum field theory in curved spacetime, a specialist subject outside the intended classical Weinberg GR exercise coverage.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 7: quantize a massive Klein-Gordon field in the printed two-dimensional cosmology whose scale factor jumps suddenly, normalize the in- and out-modes, match the field and its conjugate momentum across the jump, find the Bogoliubov coefficients, and calculate the resulting particle production.
problems.short_topic: Particle creation by a sudden cosmological expansion
problems.disposition_rationale: Although quantum, this self-contained parent gives a direct and tractable Chapter 15 illustration of particle production by cosmological time dependence.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 8: separate the Klein-Gordon equation on Schwarzschild/Kruskal spacetime into spherical harmonics and a tortoise-coordinate radial equation, derive the printed Regge-Wheeler potential, specify its self-adjoint boundary problem, and use positivity to exclude exponentially growing scalar modes.
problems.short_topic: Mode stability of a scalar field on Schwarzschild
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 8 stability parent connecting separation of variables, the effective potential, and a spectral positivity argument.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 9: use the Schwarzschild Hawking temperature to show instability in an infinite heat reservoir, then place the hole in a finite radiation reservoir of volume V, write total energy and entropy, analyze thermal extrema and stability, derive the critical volume V_c, and describe the associated phase change.
problems.short_topic: Schwarzschild black-hole thermodynamics in a finite reservoir
problems.disposition_rationale: This complete Chapter 8 thermodynamics parent makes negative heat capacity and finite-volume stabilization quantitatively explicit.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 10: determine the sign and divergence structure of the fixed-charge Reissner-Nordström heat capacity, then repeat the finite-radiation-reservoir entropy and stability analysis of Question 9, deriving the corresponding critical volume and explaining why the allowed range becomes unbounded.
problems.short_topic: Reissner-Nordström heat capacity and reservoir stability
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 8 charged-black-hole extension with an explicit dependency on Question 9's reservoir setup; both the heat-capacity calculation and revised stability range are retained.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: build projective-space coordinate charts and transition maps, realize RP^n as S^n modulo the antipodal map, identify RP^3 with SO(3), describe the stated homogeneous-space quotients, and prove CP^1 is diffeomorphic to S^2.
problems.short_topic: Real and complex projective spaces as manifolds
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a pure manifold-topology and Lie-group exercise with no substantive general-relativity application in the parent.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: determine the matrix Lie algebras of SO(n) and Sp(2n,R) from their defining bilinear forms, calculate their dimensions, and retain the sheet's requested comparison of the constraints on generators.
problems.short_topic: Lie algebras of orthogonal and symplectic groups
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent is an elementary Lie-group dimension calculation rather than a GR exercise, despite the broad usefulness of symmetry groups.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: derive the vector-field Lie bracket from the Lie derivative, prove Cartan's formula for forms, and obtain the stated identity dΩ(V,W) = V[Ω(W)] - W[Ω(V)] - Ω([V,W]) for a one-form Ω and vector fields V,W.
problems.short_topic: Lie derivatives, Cartan's formula, and exterior derivatives
problems.disposition_rationale: A self-contained Chapter 4 parent collecting three foundational differential-geometric identities used throughout relativity.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: compute invariant forms and vector fields on the Euclidean group E(2), then model the printed rear-wheel-drive car's configuration space, no-slip distribution, and controls; calculate the relevant brackets and use them to explain maneuverability and the parallel-parking motion.
problems.short_topic: Invariant geometry and nonholonomic car control
problems.disposition_rationale: The nonholonomic-control application is complete and interesting but lies outside general relativity and the target chapter collection.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 5: analyze Möbius/projective transformations on the line, identify the three-dimensional sl(2,R) subalgebra of vector fields, lift the action to T*R, and prove the stated correspondence between Lie brackets and Poisson brackets for the associated Hamiltonians.
problems.short_topic: Projective vector fields and cotangent-lift moment maps
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a symplectic/Lie-theoretic mechanics parent without a GR-specific setting, so it is retained only as out-of-scope source content.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 6: equip the semidirect-product group R_+ ⋉ R^4 with the printed left-invariant metric, identify it with the Poincaré half-space form of AdS5, give the embedding-space realization, and analyze geodesics to determine the coordinate patch's geodesic incompleteness.
problems.short_topic: Anti-de Sitter space as a Lie group half-space
problems.disposition_rationale: A Chapter 13 parent that connects group geometry, the AdS hyperboloid, and the global limitation of a commonly used coordinate patch.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 7: show that the SO(3) action on S^2 preserves the stated symplectic area form, find Hamiltonians for the infinitesimal rotation fields, and verify that their Poisson brackets reproduce the so(3) Lie algebra.
problems.short_topic: Hamiltonian SO(3) action on the two-sphere
problems.disposition_rationale: The parent is a clean symplectic moment-map exercise but does not itself develop a gravitational application.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 8: express a Poisson bracket by its antisymmetric matrix, translate the Jacobi identity into the printed component condition, prove that an invertible Poisson tensor defines a closed symplectic two-form, and analyze the special n = 1 case.
problems.short_topic: Poisson tensors and symplectic forms
problems.disposition_rationale: This is foundational Poisson geometry rather than a GR parent, and its natural home is outside the Weinberg chapter set.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 9: use the printed Beltrami-ball Hamiltonian for H^3 to construct the conserved vectors L and M, compute their full Poisson algebra and Casimirs, identify the corresponding Killing fields and so(3,1) structure, and show that unparameterized geodesics are straight chords in the ball.
problems.short_topic: Hidden symmetry and geodesics of hyperbolic three-space
problems.disposition_rationale: A substantial Chapter 13 maximally-symmetric-space parent that links geodesic dynamics, Killing symmetries, and the Lorentz algebra.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 10: identify the manifold of oriented lines in R^(n+1) with TS^n, and for n = 2 carry out the printed mini-twistor coordinate maps, group-action/orbit description, and quotient to unoriented lines.
problems.short_topic: Geometry and mini-twistor description of oriented lines
problems.disposition_rationale: This is twistor/incidence geometry with no direct classical-GR exercise developed in the parent.

problems.short_topic: Bogomolny bound for two-dimensional sigma models

problems.disposition_rationale: The calculation is a gauge-theory/topology parent outside classical GR, although all normalizations remain recorded for source fidelity.

problems.short_topic: Self-dual two-forms and the so(4) decomposition
problems.disposition_rationale: The exercise develops Euclidean gauge-theory representation identities rather than a GR curvature application.
